name: How deep down
question: Meters below the water surface. Each gridline step is ten times deeper.

items.name: Recreational scuba limit
items.fact: Below about 30 m, nitrogen starts to make divers feel drunk.

items.name: Deep Dive Dubai pool
items.fact: Deep Dive Dubai has a sunken city at the bottom of the pool.

items.name: Kursk submarine wreck
items.fact: The Kursk sank in the Barents Sea in 2000.

items.name: Where sunlight fades out
items.fact: Below about 200 m there isn't enough light for photosynthesis.

items.name: Free-dive record (no limits)
items.fact: Herbert Nitsch reached 214 m on a single breath in 2007.

items.name: Deepest scuba dive
items.fact: The record dive took 12 minutes down and almost 14 hours back up.

items.name: Lake Tahoe (deepest point)
items.fact: Lake Tahoe is so clear you can see down about 20 m.

items.name: Emperor penguin dive
items.fact: Emperor penguins can hold their breath for over 20 minutes.

items.name: Crater Lake (deepest point)
items.fact: Crater Lake is the deepest lake in the United States.

items.name: Leatherback turtle dive
items.fact: Leatherbacks are the largest living turtles.

items.name: Lake Baikal (deepest point)
items.fact: Lake Baikal holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh water.

items.name: Sperm whale dive
items.fact: Sperm whales dive deep to hunt giant squid.

items.name: Cuvier's beaked whale dive
items.fact: One Cuvier's beaked whale stayed under for 3 hours 42 minutes.

items.name: Average ocean depth
items.fact: The average ocean is deeper than most mountains on land are tall.

items.name: Titanic wreck
items.fact: The Titanic's wreck was found in 1985, 73 years after it sank.

items.name: Puerto Rico Trench
items.fact: The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest point of the Atlantic.

items.name: Challenger Deep
items.fact: The pressure in Challenger Deep is over 1,000 times that at the surface.
